messages.subject: Sex-specific RSF layers to evaluate density
messages.subject_clean: Sex-specific RSF layers to evaluate density
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I would like to evaluate an existing male RSF layer and a female RSF layer in comparison to density.  Is there a way to set up a single model such that the male RSF is applied to males only and the female RSF is applied to females only?  It is similar to an interaction, but I'm not sure if an interaction would work for this.  Also, is there a way to handle individuals of unknown sex in this process?

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Hi Elizabeth, sorry for missing this message as Google sent it to spam for me.

I don't see how to apply the RSF covariate in this sex-specific way aside from fitting entirely separate models for each sex.  The problem with that is then you lose the ability to include unknown sex individuals (which is part of oSCR's appeal).

How many unknown sex individuals are there?  Would hate to throw away data, but you could make the argument that the unknown sex captures are not helping you understand sex-specific differences anyway.  You could also assume that sex identification is random, such that individuals with sex identified are a representative sample of your population and therefore sufficient to making the inferences you desire.

Elizabeth
